title: Deployment and Scaling Patterns
description: Deploy RAG, MCP, and agent backends with scalable .NET hosting, caching, and resilience patterns.

blocks.text: AI workloads differ from traditional APIs because they are latency-sensitive, cost-sensitive, and often stateful. Deployment design should account for caching, connection pooling, model access patterns, and graceful degradation.

blocks.title: Common deployment shapes
items: **Monolithic ASP.NET Core app** — simplest path for small to medium workloads.
**Sidecar services** — separate retrieval, embedding, and generation services for independent scaling.
**Background workers** — precompute embeddings and refresh indexes asynchronously.
**Serverless APIs** — good for bursty traffic with cold-start tolerance.

blocks.title: Resilience controls
items: **Retry with backoff** — retry transient provider failures safely.
**Circuit breaker** — avoid overwhelming a failing model or retrieval service.
**Timeout budgets** — bound end-to-end latency for user-facing requests.
**Fallbacks** — return cached answers or simplified responses when AI services degrade.

blocks.title: Polly resilience for AI endpoints
blocks.content: Retry, timeout, and circuit-breaker policies for external AI service calls.

blocks.title: Design for degradation
blocks.text: If your LLM or vector store is unavailable, the backend should still respond. Prefer cached or simplified responses over errors.

items.text: I can describe a hosting topology for AI workloads
items.hint: Monolith, sidecars, background workers, or serverless depending on scale

items.text: I implement timeouts and retries for external AI calls
items.hint: Use Polly or equivalent patterns in ASP.NET Core

items.text: I have a fallback strategy for degraded services
items.hint: Return cached or simplified responses instead of crashing

blocks.title: Lesson Summary
points: AI backends need deployment topologies that match their latency and cost profiles.
Resilience, caching, and fallback behavior are required for production.
ASP.NET Core supports all required hosting models.
blocks.takeaway: Production AI is an infrastructure problem as much as a model problem. Deploy for failure, not just for success.
